validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, real and well-documented, from the sheet's own wiki citation list (never cited directly, read for leads only per standing rule 1). Two genuinely independent origins agree in detail: (1) http://www.cnpc-amg.kz/data/transgaz/111.pdf, an internal technical asset sheet titled 'Магистральный газопровод Жанажол-КС13' published on AO SNPS-Aktobemunaigas's own domain, signed by their PTO USN i NP department head (Serkeshtaev T.M.) -- this PDF is a scanned image (pdftotext returns nothing; pdfimages -list shows a 200ppi full-page JPEG on page 2), so url_verifier's automated content screen cannot see inside it (a known false-negative class per its own docstring for image-based/large PDFs) -- I rendered both pages to PNG (pdftoppm -r 200) and read them directly: it gives length 157.4 km, diameter 813 mm, design pressure 6.4 MPa, design throughput 5.2 bcm/y, commissioned 2006, 8 linear valve stations, head station at Zhanazhol field, end station near Kaindy village at Compressor Station No.13 of the Bukhara-Ural line, entirely within Mugalzharsky District, Aktobe Region; and (2) https://kase.kz/ru/news/show/181180/, a dated (06.10.2005) KASE-hosted press release from the same company describing a construction-completion ceremony on 5 Oct 2005 for 'gazoprovod Zhanazhol-KS-13', $95M USD invested, ~156 km, ~5 bcm/y capacity, construction started 2004, explicitly connecting the Zhanazhol field to the Bukhara-Ural trunk line and gasifying Aktobe-region settlements (Emba, Zhem, Yubileynoye, Birlik, Kumzhargan). A THIRD, genuinely independent origin -- the actual pipeline OPERATOR, AO Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya, in its own 2015 annual report (https://kase.kz/files/emitters/INCA/incap_2015_rus.pdf, 128pp, verified 200 via url_verifier but the automated content screen misses deep pages on a 20MB/128pp PDF -- manually confirmed via `pdftotext -layout` + grep) -- lists 'Жанажол-КС-13' among the trunk pipelines operated by its UMG Aktobe branch (alongside Bukhara-Ural, Zhanazhol-Oktyabrsk-Aktobe, Kartaly-Rudny-Kostanay, Beyneu-Bozoy-Shymkent), gives an operating-inventory table row (commissioned 2007, 156 km, 5.2 bcm/y design, 3.848 bcm actual 2015 throughput, 74% utilization), and states explicitly it is a third-party-owned asset it services under contract. Three independent orgs (AktobeMunaiGas, KASE's newswire, Intergas TsA) describing the same physical pipe with matching length/diameter/capacity/route is unambiguous confirmation this is a real, existing, operating asset -- not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct. Every source calls it a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk/main gas pipeline) carrying processed ('товарный') gas from the Zhanazhol gas-processing complex into the national grid -- Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both well supported, this is not a gathering/feeder line despite its short length (157 km is simply the true distance from the Zhanazhol field to the nearest trunk-line tie-in). DUPLICATE: checked against the full 39-pipeline Kazakhstan-gas roster. No match found -- P3944 'Zhanazhol-Aktobe/Zhanazhol-Oktyabrsk-Aktobe' (len 270, cap 0.7) is a DIFFERENT, separately-documented physical line in the same Intergas UMG-Aktobe list (Intergas AR2015's own table gives it 143 km / 0.697 bcm/y, distinct from this row's 156-157.4 km / 5.2 bcm/y), and P3946 'Kozhasai-KS12' is a different field-to-trunk feeder entirely. GulfPub's crosswalk match ('Zhanazhol - Taldyk', 156.11 km) is the same physical pipe as P3945 (156ish km, same origin field), not a separate GEM-tracked entity -- no double-count risk.

This is an explicit, unambiguous ownership statement from the operator itself -- a different, independent organization from AktobeMunaiGas -- naming AktobeMunaiGas, not QazaqGaz/Intergas/KazTransGas, as owner. It is corroborated implicitly by the fact that the technical asset description (cnpc-amg.kz/data/transgaz/111.pdf) is hosted on AktobeMunaiGas's own domain and authored by their internal engineering department (Nachalnik PTO USN i NP), consistent with a company documenting its own capital asset. Note the Operator field (Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya) is CORRECT and independently self-confirmed by the same 2015 AR passage -- this is purely an Owner-field defect, an owner/operator split (AktobeMunaiGas owns; Intergas TsA operates under a service contract), not a wrong Operator.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently records EndState/Province=Osh, EndCountryOrArea=Kazakhstan, EndPrefecture/District=Taldyk. Osh is a city/region in KYRGYZSTAN, ~1,500 km from this pipeline's actual route and administratively unconnected to it -- a hard geographic error (EndCountryOrArea correctly says Kazakhstan, so this looks like a mismatched province pulled from elsewhere, not a country mix-up). Two independent primary sources place the entire route, start to end, within Mugalzharsky District, Aktobe Region: (1) cnpc-amg.kz's technical sheet states outright under 'Месторасположение': 'Мугалжарский район... Начинается от Головной станции в/п. Жанажол, проходит по землям Батпаккольского сельского округа, Кумжарганского аульского округа, г. Эмбы, Каиндинского сельского округа и заканчивается на Конечной станции около Компрессорной станции №13 МГ «Бухара-Урал» п. Каинды' (starts at Zhanazhol wellfield, crosses Batpakkol/Kumzhargan rural districts and the town of Emba, ends at the Final Station near Compressor Station No.13 of the Bukhara-Ural line, at Kaindy village) -- the true end locality is KAINDY, not Osh and not (per this source) Taldyk; (2) Intergas TsA's 2015 annual report states its UMG Aktobe branch's whole network, explicitly including Zhanazhol-KS-13, runs 'по территориям Актюбинской и Кустанайской областей' (through the territories of Aktobe and Kostanay oblasts) -- Kyrgyzstan's Osh is nowhere in this picture. I checked whether 'Taldyk' (EndPrefecture/District) is at least a real, nearby place: there IS a village called Талдык in Aktobe Region, but it sits in the Aitekebiysky district, a DIFFERENT, non-adjacent-to-the-route district from Mugalzharsky where both primary sources place this pipeline's entire length -- so even if 'Taldyk' isn't purely fabricated, it does not match the documented terminus (Kaindy/Mugalzharsky). GulfPub's independent crosswalk match is itself labeled 'Zhanazhol - Taldyk' (156.11 km) -- so GEM's 'Taldyk' likely came from that same secondary source rather than from either primary document; I could not independently confirm or refute it as the precise end locality and am flagging it for a closer look rather than asserting a specific replacement, but EndState/Province='Osh' is confidently wrong regardless of how the district question resolves.

validity.recommendation: No change recommended to StartYear1=2006, but flag the three-source year spread in ResearcherNotes rather than treating it as settled: construction-completion ceremony Oct 2005 (KASE/AktobeMunaiGas press release) vs 'введен в эксплуатацию в 2006' (AktobeMunaiGas's own technical sheet, matching GEM) vs commissioning year 2007 in Intergas TsA's 2015 annual-report inventory table.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM: StartYear1=2006. AktobeMunaiGas's own technical document states 'Введен в эксплуатацию в 2006г.' -- an exact match, and the most authoritative single source for the owner's own declared start-of-operations date. But two other dated data points complicate a clean 'confirmed': the KASE press release (dated 06.10.2005) describes a formal completion-of-construction ceremony held 5 October 2005 ('состоялась торжественная церемония завершения строительства газопровода Жанажол-КС-13'); and Intergas TsA's 2015 annual-report operating-inventory table lists this line's commissioning year as 2007, not 2006. These three dates (2005 construction complete / 2006 owner-declared start / 2007 operator-inventory commissioning) most likely reflect three different real milestones -- construction finished, AktobeMunaiGas's own start-of-service date, and the point at which Intergas TsA's inventory system dates its operational takeover under the service contract -- rather than one of them being simply wrong. Since GEM's value matches the owner's own explicit 'введен в эксплуатацию' statement, I am not recommending a change, but the disagreement is real and material enough (a different year, from the pipeline's actual current operator) that it should not be read as fully closed.

summary: P3945 (Zhanazhol-KS13) is real, correctly classified, and not a duplicate -- confirmed high-confidence by three independent origins (AktobeMunaiGas's own technical sheet, a 2005 KASE press release, and Intergas TsA's 2015 annual report), with length/diameter/capacity/cost/status all corroborated and 11 refs staged as REFS_ADDED. Two attribution concerns raised for Update: Owner1 should likely be AO SNPS-Aktobemunaigas, not QazaqGaz (Intergas TsA's own AR names AktobeMunaiGas as the third-party owner it services under contract); and EndState/Province='Osh' is a clear geographic error (Osh is in Kyrgyzstan) -- the pipeline runs entirely within Mugalzharsky District, Aktobe Region, terminating at Kaindy village near KS-13, so EndState/Province should read 'Aktobe' and EndPrefecture/District='Taldyk' needs re-verification. A minor spec caveat on StartYear1 (2006 vs a conflicting 2007 in Intergas's own inventory table) is noted but not recommended for change. Nothing UNRESOLVED among the fills staged.
